title: Cohost memory overhead and TTL sensitivity matrix (Q2 2026)
body:
Purpose
Provide a compact spreadsheet-style sensitivity analysis for multi-model cohosting on the GPU fleet. Focus is on how per-request KV cache retention TTLs and model co-residency ratios change in-flight memory pressure, required GPU headroom, and cross-region staging needs. This is meant to inform rollout cadence limits and warmup strategies for models with large KV footprints.

Executive summary (short)
- TTLs matter: increasing KV retention from 30s to 300s increases memory pressure per pod by ~3.5x for our traffic mix, raising required headroom by 15-40% across regions.
- Co-residency risk: cohosting high-KV models at >25% of a GPU's active lanes doubles eviction churn and can increase tail latency. Recommend limiting cohost fraction per GPU by class.
- Mitigation knobs: aggressive TTL dialing by model class, per-model lane isolation, and prewarm shadowing reduce cold-starts and lower required preprovisioning.

Assumptions and constants used in sheet
- baseline sequence distribution: p50=128, p90=512, p99=1024 tokens.
- KV per token stored: 0.28 KB/token for dense transformer keys after compression.
- Average request KV retention = seq_len * KV_per_token * retention_factor (where retention_factor accounts for internal caching of prefixes).
- GPU memory available to runtime per machine class: small-gpu=40GB usable, medium-gpu=72GB, large-gpu=120GB.
- Baseline model mix for rollout scenario: 60% small-KV models, 30% medium-KV, 10% large-KV.
- Co-residency ratios considered: 10%, 25%, 50% active lanes occupied by large-KV models.

Sheet: TTL sensitivity matrix (rows are TTL buckets, columns are regional summaries)
Columns: TTL bucket | avg KV per active request (KB) | estimated per-GPU KV memory delta (GB) | extra GPUs required for 20% buffer (us-west1) | extra GPUs required for 20% buffer (europe-west3) | extra GPUs required for 20% buffer (asia-east1) | notes
Rows (example values):
- TTL 30s | 18 KB | 1.1 GB | 2 | 3 | 3 | short retention, minimal cold-hit reuse, cohost risk moderate
- TTL 60s | 32 KB | 2.0 GB | 3 | 4 | 4 | moderate reuse improves p99 slightly but memory doubles
- TTL 120s | 58 KB | 3.6 GB | 5 | 6 | 7 | good reuse for chat scenarios, heavy memory hit for medium/large models
- TTL 300s | 96 KB | 5.8 GB | 8 | 10 | 11 | long retention pushes many GPUs to scale out unless lanes isolated

Key calculation snippets (spreadsheet formulas expressed in plain text)
- avg_kv_per_req_kb = seq_len_p50 * kv_per_token_kb * retention_multiplier_by_ttl
- per_gpu_kv_gb = avg_kv_per_req_kb * expected_concurrent_requests_per_gpu / 1024
- extra_gpus_for_buffer = ceil((baseline_per_gpu_kv_gb + per_gpu_kv_gb)*1.2 / usable_gpu_memory_gb) - baseline_gpus_allocated
Notes: expected_concurrent_requests_per_gpu varies by region and machine class; we used 18 for small-gpu, 40 for medium, 70 for large in this sheet.

Cohosting scenarios evaluated (three canonical scenarios)
1) Conservative: limit large-KV models to 10% of active lanes. Result: TTL 120s -> extra 2-4 GPUs per region. p99 latency impact minimal.
2) Mixed: 25% cohost. Result: TTL 120s -> extra 5-8 GPUs per region; tail latency increases during transient spikes without lane isolation.
3) Aggressive: 50% cohost. Result: TTL 120s -> extra 12-16 GPUs per region; eviction churn spikes, time-to-stabilize after rollout ~18-24 minutes observed in trace sims.

Regional breakdown commentary
- us-west1: traffic skewed to short sessions and read-heavy requests; TTL increases provide less reuse but memory still grows. Lower baseline concurrency reduces per-GPU delta but limited spare capacity.
- europe-west3: steady long chat sessions drive higher KV retention benefits but require more headroom to avoid eviction thrash.
- asia-east1: highest p99 sensitivity due to vertical stacking of business-critical tenants; recommend stricter cohost limits there.

Operational recommendations
- Rollout throttle policy by TTL category: allow staged rollout caps based on measured KV pressure, e.g., start with 10% cohost for first 24h, move to 25% only after error and p99 checks.
- Per-model TTL profiling job: add a CI job that returns an empirical retention_multiplier_by_ttl by replaying sampled request traces for each model. Use that value in provisioning calculators.
- Lane affinity labeling: mark lanes as low, medium, high KV capacity and only schedule large-KV models on high-KV lanes. Implement via runtime placement hints.
- Fast bailout for tails: if eviction-driven CPU or GPU stalls detected, automatically reduce TTL to next lower bucket for affected models for 30m.
- Prewarm shadowing: run 1% traffic to a shadow pool with full TTL to prepopulate KV and reduce cold miss pressure during canary.

Open questions and risks
- measurement noise in TTL profiling makes headroom estimates uncertain by +/- 20%. Need systematic sampling across peak/off-peak windows.
- multi-tenant QoS interactions when a single tenant runs many medium-KV models concurrently. Possible need for per-tenant lane reservation.
- billing and cost attribution: longer TTLs reduce per-token compute but raise infrastructure commit costs; need finance input on break-even TTL for reserved capacity.

Immediate next steps (owners)
- CI profiling job proto: Marco Liu by 2026-03-15.
- Implement lane affinity labels in scheduler prototype: Aisha Patel + infra team by 2026-03-22.
- Run 3-region trace replay to validate matrix numbers: Sofia Ortega by 2026-03-18.
- Raise JIRA-INF-2148 to track rollout throttles and config toggles: Devon Park (owner).

Appendix: quick numbers snapshot used for estimates
- kv_per_token_kb = 0.28
- retention_multiplier_by_ttl lookup used: TTL30=1.2, TTL60=2.0, TTL120=3.5, TTL300=6.0
- expected_concurrent_requests_per_gpu: small=18, medium=40, large=70
- baseline_gpus_allocated for region (example): us-west1=1200, europe-west3=900, asia-east1=650
- example computed impact for TTL120 and mixed cohost (25% large-KV): additional 5 GPUs per 100 baseline in us-west1 equivalent.

If you want, I can produce a CSV export of the table rows with the raw numeric columns for import into the capacity planner spreadsheet.
